audit.summary: Theorem 3.1 is false at the explicit tau=1 hitting-time parameter; rare-state splitting does not preserve a fixed hitting bound. Algorithm 1 fails to maintain the weighted-gradient invariant used in the central convergence proof. A separate local TD-gradient reformulation is invalid.

Limitations: The algorithm invariant repair is verified algebraically, not as a repaired convergence theorem.

P1 — Hitting-time class contradicts Theorem 3.1 — Counterevidence: Mixing time one would allow nontrivial iid sampling, but the displayed class uses hitting time. No repaired theorem under a different parameter is certified.

P2 — Printed MaC-SAGE recurrence differs from proof invariant — Counterevidence: The intended weighted-gradient algorithm might admit a bound. This finite counterexample does not prove divergence or refute every possible rate analysis of the printed recursion.
P2 — Printed MaC-SAGE recurrence differs from proof invariant — Limit: Remaining convergence proof not validated.
P3 — TD vector field lacks the claimed scalar potential — Counterevidence: Conservative fields or special expected TD fields can have potentials; neither establishes the claimed per-sample identity.
Limitations: Focused acceptance of reported issues only; initial full-paper coverage is not claimed as independently repeated.

proposition.claim:
For all positive parameters, including tau=1, Ns has a positive epsilon^-4 lower-bound term.

The displayed recurrence maintains G_t=sum_i y_t^i h_t^i.

The line integral f has gradient equal to the per-sample TD vector field g.

assumptions: tau_hit maximizes expected positive hitting/return time over all pairs; stationary unbiasedness and variance upper bound; L-smooth F with gap <=Delta; zero-respecting algorithms.
Two iid states of equal stationary probability; f1=x^2/2+x, f2=x^2/2-x; L=sigma=1, Delta=1, tau=2; zero initialization; gamma0=1/8; positive-probability state path 1,2.
Two states with features e1,e2, zero reward, gamma=1/2, theta*=0; iid chain has positive probability of the transition e1 to e2; theta0=0.
